opening_silence.text: Don't do this again. Not tonight.

2.text: The doctor came again. Third time tonight. That's not a good number.
He asked if the family was all here. I said almost.

3.text: They're letting me sit next to him now.
His breathing sounds like waves. The nurse said that's normal. Normal.

options.text: aman told me. he saw you at the hospital last week
reply: Aman.
He was here Tuesday. Sat with Papa for an hour so I could go wash my face.

silence.text: Someone should have told you. There. I said it.

options.text: how is he
reply: Not good.
They moved him to the ICU around 11. His pressure keeps dropping and coming back.

options.text: is he awake
reply: In and out. More out.
He's sedated. It's easier when he's sedated. For him I mean.

options.text: i'm at the gate. boarding in 40 minutes
reply: Okay.
Good.

options.text: my phone's at 4 and i have the wrong adapter. it's going to die
reply: Then don't spend it on me.

options.text: why didn't you tell me. any of you. i had to hear my own father is dying from aman
reply: You changed the number.

silence.text: I tried the old one anyway. In March.
A man in Noida answered. He was nice about it. Said people call for you sometimes.

options.text: where's ma
reply: Asleep in the family room. I put my shawl over her.
She won't lie down properly. Keeps her chappals on. Ready to run somewhere I suppose.

options.text: i land at 9:10. straight to the hospital from there
reply: Montu will get you. Gate 2.
He still has the same car. You'll see it and feel like nothing changed. Then you'll get here.

options.text: i'm sorry
reply: For which part.

options.text: what did the doctor actually say. tell me straight
reply: Three days ago they asked us whether to keep going with the full treatment. All of it.
I said no. I decided on the stairwell outside radiology. I had about four minutes and a paper cup of chai.

silence.text: Good. It deserves a bit of quiet.

options.text: you made the right call didi
reply: I didn't need it to be right.
I needed to not be the only one in the stairwell. That's all I needed.

options.text: you shouldn't have had to decide that alone. i should have been in that stairwell with you
reply: Yes.
Well.
You're in an airport. It's a start.

options.text: you knew where i live. aman knows. you could have reached me any time you wanted
reply: I know your building. I know the flat number. I know your Sunday market.
Knowing was never the problem.

options.text: are you ok
reply: I'm fine.

silence.text: No one's asked me that since February, actually.
Fine is the wrong word. Upright. I'm upright and I know where the good bathroom is to cry in.
Sixth floor, past the chemist. For your information. For tomorrow.

options.text: have you eaten anything
reply: There's a machine downstairs that makes something brown.
I've had four. Meena bua brought parathas at midnight but nobody could.

options.text: does papa know i'm coming
reply: No.
I'll tell him when your plane is actually in the air. I've stopped giving him things that might not arrive.

options.text: can you video call for one minute. i just want to see his face
reply: Your phone would die on the ringing screen.
And not like this. You'll see him with your own eyes in six hours. That's the version he'd want.

options.text: they're calling my boarding group
reply: Go. Sit near the front.
Every minute matters on the other side.

options.text: how long are they saying. honestly
reply: They stopped saying numbers on Tuesday.
It stopped being weeks a while ago. Tonight it stopped being days. So.

options.text: then why
reply: Papa told us not to.
He said if you wanted to know us, you knew the number.
I told him it was cruel. He said so was leaving.

options.text: for leaving the way i left. for the number. for making aman do this family's job for three years
reply: Thank you.
That's all I wanted. The list. Someone else holding the list for a minute.

options.text: aman told me three weeks ago. i've had the ticket open in a tab for three weeks. i couldn't press buy. i don't know what was wrong with me
reply: Three weeks.
You pressed it tonight.
That's the version I'm keeping. Don't argue with me about it.

options.text: i didn't leave to hurt anyone. staying was turning me into someone i didn't want you to meet
reply: I know.
I always knew. That was the part I couldn't explain to him.

options.text: i'm scared didi
reply: me too
First time anyone in this family has said that out loud, I think.

options.text: we take off in a few minutes. it's real now. you can tell him. please tell him
reply: Telling him now.
I'm holding his hand and saying it. His eyebrows moved.
He heard me. He heard it.

options.text: what happens to you after all this. have you thought about you at all
reply: I don't let myself.
One corridor at a time.

options.text: i'm not disappearing again. whatever happens in the morning i'm staying. i mean it this time
reply: We'll see.
I would like that to be a true sentence.

waits.text: I can see your dots starting and stopping. Type the thing.
The corridor smells like phenyl and someone's marigolds. There's a puja going in the next ward.
He checks the weather where you are. Every night after the news. He knew it rained on you yesterday.
His hand keeps doing the two finger tap. Like he's checking the shop shutter one more time.
Don't save the battery. Whatever you're saving it for, this is the thing it was for.

messages: He's surfacing. The nurse says a few minutes, maybe.
I'm going in. Give me one thing to carry. Quick.

options.text: i love you
tell him i'm coming home
tell him i'm sorry. he'll know for what
don't tell him anything. just hold his hand and don't let go until i'm there. that one's from me

delivered_reply: He heard. His eyes are open. He's trying to say something back, wait, he wants me to type it exactly, he's saying
